mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and increase the attractiveness of equities relative to fixed income.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5.0%, the S&P 500 is expected to produce negative forward 20-day returns due to heightened concerns about monetary tightening and its impact on corporate borrowing costs and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the annualized change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.0% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, the S&P 500 is expected to produce negative forward 20-day returns due to a combination of high inflation and restrictive monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both CPIAUCSL (annualized change) > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During recessions (defined by negative quarterly GDP growth, GDPC1), the S&P 500 is expected to produce negative forward 60-day returns due to deteriorating corporate earnings and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative during periods when GDPC1 (quarterly growth) < 0.0% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns, as elevated unemployment signals weak economic conditions and reduced consumer spending, leading to lower equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is above 4.5% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110.0 (an index level indicating a slowdown), the S&P 500 is expected to produce negative forward 5-day returns due to concerns about economic contraction and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 110.0 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200.0 and industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 115.0, the S&P 500 is expected to produce negative forward 60-day returns due to a confluence of weak consumer demand (low housing starts) and reduced industrial activity (low INDPRO).
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both HOUST < 1200.0 and INDPRO < 115.0 (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%), the S&P 500 is expected to produce negative forward 20-day returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings pressure, as reflected in the unemployment rate.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 5.0% (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
